title: A complex 2-state 3-color Turing machine is likely the simplest universal one

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A complex 2-state 3-color Turing machine is likely the simplest universal one

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The 2-state 3-color Turing machine numbered 596,440, which yields complicated behavior from a blank tape, is likely universal, and if so would by most measures be the simplest universal Turing machine.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And although it will no doubt be very difficult to prove, it seems likely that this Turing machine will in the end turn out to be universal. And if so, then presumably it will by most measures be the very simplest Turing machine that is universal.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 11, “The Notion of Computation”; section “Universality in Turing Machines and Other Systems” (from p. 706), p. 709. Scope: 2-state 3-color Turing machines

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch11-30: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The target machine is finite and fully specified, but bounded computation cannot settle universality. The secondary minimality claim also requires exhaustive nonuniversality results for smaller machine classes.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Provide a universal-machine simulation encoded in machine 596,440 or prove an invariant excluding universality, then compare its state-symbol size under a fixed minimality measure with all smaller machines.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Complex blank-tape behavior is not evidence sufficient for universality.

A universality proof or obstruction is missing.

'Simplest' varies across machine-size measures and conventions.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A detailed public proof, later machine-checked in parts, addresses the universality of this specific machine, so that conjunct is open to audit now. Whether the machine is the simplest depends on the size measure and on open neighbors such as 3-state 2-color machines, which a 2-state 2-color classification does not close. The claim as a conjunction is therefore only partly decided.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Check a reduction from cyclic tag systems or Turing machines to machine 596,440, including the initial-condition encoding. Universality is confirmed if every computation is emulated and the encoding itself is not doing the computation. Simplest is confirmed only relative to a stated size measure and a completed proof that every smaller machine is non-universal.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The proof uses a non-periodic infinite initial condition, so it can be rejected by a definition of universality that requires a periodic background.

By most measures is undefined, and 3-state 2-color machines have the same number of transitions and are not fully classified.
